units.title: Angular geometry on the actual unit sphere
units.classification: canonical shared library node; original mathematical supplement
units.statement: Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure, and let S be its literal unit-norm subtype. The actual angular cost c(u,v)=arccos(inner(u,v)) is jointly continuous and measurable on S×S. For every pair it lies between zero and pi, equals Mathlib's unoriented vector angle, dominates the ambient chord norm, vanishes exactly on the diagonal, and is symmetric. It satisfies the triangle inequality. These are explicit properties of the angular cost; no inherited chord-distance instance is replaced, no path-length geodesic-distance identification or Wasserstein theorem is included, and no sphere nonemptiness or positive dimension is assumed.
units.formula: c(u,v)=\arccos\langle u,v\rangle,\quad 0\le c\le\pi,\quad \|u-v\|\le c(u,v),\quad c(u,w)\le c(u,v)+c(v,w).
assumptions: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space with its Borel measurable structure.
S is exactly the unit-norm subtype and c(u,v)=arccos(inner(u,v)). Neither positive dimension nor a point of S is assumed.

steps.title: Identify the angle
steps.text: Unit norms cancel the denominator in the vector-angle definition, so the literal arccos cost is the existing unoriented angle. Continuity follows from continuous subtype coercions, the inner product and arccos; finite dimension supplies second countability for the measurable product.
steps.lean:
have heq (u v : {w : E // ‖w‖ = 1}) :
      Real.arccos ⟪u.1,v.1⟫_ℝ = InnerProductGeometry.angle u.1 v.1 := by
    simp [InnerProductGeometry.angle,u.property,v.property]
  have hc : Continuous (fun z : {w : E // ‖w‖ = 1} × {w : E // ‖w‖ = 1} =>
      Real.arccos ⟪z.1.1,z.2.1⟫_ℝ) := by fun_prop

steps.title: Compare a chord with its angle
steps.text: Set θ=c(u,v)=angle(u,v). For unit endpoints, expand the squared chord norm. The half-angle identity and sin squared bounded by its argument squared yield the chord estimate; both norms and the angle are nonnegative.
steps.lean:
private theorem chord_le_angle
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    (u v : E) (hu : ‖u‖ = 1) (hv : ‖v‖ = 1) :
    ‖u-v‖ ≤ InnerProductGeometry.angle u v := by
  let θ := InnerProductGeometry.angle u v
  have hθ : 0 ≤ θ := InnerProductGeometry.angle_nonneg u v
  have hc : Real.cos θ = ⟪u,v⟫_ℝ := by
    simpa [θ,hu,hv] using InnerProductGeometry.cos_angle u v
  have heq : ‖u-v‖^2 = 2-2*Real.cos θ := by
    rw [norm_sub_sq_real,hu,hv,hc]
    ring
  have hh := Real.sin_sq_eq_half_sub (θ/2)
  have htwo : 2*(θ/2) = θ := by ring
  rw [htwo] at hh
  have hs := Real.sin_sq_le_sq (x := θ/2)
  change ‖u-v‖ ≤ θ
  nlinarith [norm_nonneg (u-v)]

steps.title: Separate points and record the range
steps.text: The principal arccos lies in [0,pi]. A zero cost forces zero chord, hence equal subtype points. Conversely every unit vector is nonzero and has zero angle with itself. Inner-product symmetry supplies cost symmetry.
steps.lean:
refine ⟨Real.arccos_nonneg _,Real.arccos_le_pi _,heq u v,hchord,?_,?_⟩
    · constructor
      · intro hz
        apply Subtype.ext
        apply sub_eq_zero.mp
        apply norm_eq_zero.mp
        exact le_antisymm (by simpa only [hz] using hchord) (norm_nonneg _)
      · rintro rfl
        rw [heq]
        apply InnerProductGeometry.angle_self
        intro hz
        have hh := u.property
        rw [hz,norm_zero] at hh
        norm_num at hh
    · rw [heq,heq,InnerProductGeometry.angle_comm]

steps.title: Use the vector-angle triangle inequality
steps.text: Replace each literal cost by its angle expression and apply the existing vector-angle triangle inequality. This is an angular-cost fact; it does not identify an intrinsic path-length metric, particularly on the disconnected two-point sphere.
steps.lean:
· intro u v w
    rw [heq,heq,heq]
    exact InnerProductGeometry.angle_le_angle_add_angle u.1 v.1 w.1

units.title: Uniform gradients of quadratic feature-law potentials
units.classification: canonical shared library node; original mathematical supplement
units.statement: Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space with its Borel measurable structure and H a complete real inner-product normed space. Let F:E→H have actual ambient Frechet derivative D(w):E→H for every w. Assume nonnegative M1,M2, an operator bound norm(D(w))<=M1 on the closed unit ball and an operator-Lipschitz bound norm(D(w)-D(u))<=M2 norm(w-u) there. Fix y in H. On the actual unit-norm subtype S define K(w)=F(w), angular cost c(u,v)=arccos(inner(u,v)), the actual Bochner mean m(mu)=integral K dmu, V_mu(w)=2 inner(m(mu)-y,F(w)), and G_mu(w)=2P_w D(w)^*(m(mu)-y) with the explicit projection P_w z=z−⟨z,w⟩w, which projects onto w-perpendicular when norm(w)=1. Let Q(mu,nu) be the literal extended nonnegative infimum of the quadratic angular cost over all actual couplings. There exist C1,C2>0, independent of probability laws and unit weights, such that for every actual parameter probability K is integrable, V_mu has the displayed ambient gradient 2D(w)^*(m(mu)-y) at every ambient w, and its projected G_mu is tangent and uniformly bounded by C1 at every unit weight. For every two actual parameter probabilities Q is finite and norm(G_mu(w)-G_nu(u))<=C2*(sqrt(Q).toReal+c(w,u)). Feature boundedness, strong measurability, feature Lipschitz control and residual budgets are derived inside the proof rather than assumed; the returned conclusions are feature integrability, actual ambient gradient, tangency/uniform bound, finite transport cost and the joint sensitivity estimate. The constants may depend on the displayed feature/derivative data, E,H and y. This is a generic feature-law theorem, not a concrete Gaussian scalar-data potential, installed manifold-gradient/Wasserstein API or intrinsic path-length theorem.
units.formula: P_wz=z-\langle z,w\rangle w,\quad V_\mu(w)=2\langle m_\mu-y,F(w)\rangle,\quad G_\mu(w)=2P_wD(w)^*(m_\mu-y),\quad \|G_\mu(w)-G_\nu(u)\|\le C_2\bigl(Q(\mu,\nu)^{1/2}+c(w,u)\bigr).
assumptions: E is finite-dimensional real Hilbert with Borel structure; H is a complete real inner-product normed space, with no separability assumption.
F:E→H has actual full ambient Frechet derivative D(w) at every w. M1,M2≥0 bound the derivative operator norm and its operator Lipschitz increment on the closed unit ball.
y is fixed. S is the literal unit-norm subtype; m is the actual Bochner integral, c the literal arccos cost, and Q the infimum of angular squared cost over all actual couplings.

steps.title: Produce feature continuity and chord control
steps.text: Differentiability gives continuity. The convex mean-value bound on the closed unit ball produces the M1 chord Lipschitz estimate. Continuity on a second-countable domain yields strong measurability of the feature restriction even when H is not separable.
steps.lean:
have hFc : Continuous F := continuous_iff_continuousAt.mpr fun w => (hF w).continuousAt
  have hKsm : StronglyMeasurable K := (hFc.comp continuous_subtype_val).stronglyMeasurable
  have hChord (w u : E) (hw : ‖w‖ ≤ 1) (hu : ‖u‖ ≤ 1) :
      ‖F w-F u‖ ≤ M₁*‖w-u‖ := by
    apply (convex_closedBall (0 : E) 1).norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_hasFDerivWithin_le
      (fun z _ => (hF z).hasFDerivWithinAt) ?_
      (by simpa [Metric.mem_closedBall,dist_zero_right] using hu)
      (by simpa [Metric.mem_closedBall,dist_zero_right] using hw)
    intro z hz
    exact hBound z (by simpa [Metric.mem_closedBall,dist_zero_right] using hz)

steps.title: Produce one uniform feature bound
steps.text: Compare every unit feature with F(0), using the previous estimate and the norm triangle inequality. The extra one makes B a convenient positive budget. This budget is an internal consequence, not a new premise.
steps.lean:
let B := ‖F (0:E)‖+M₁+1
  have hB : 0 ≤ B := by dsimp [B]; positivity
  have hKb (w : S) : ‖K w‖ ≤ B := by
    have hb := hChord w.1 0 w.property.le (by simp)
    have hn := norm_add_le (F w.1-F 0) (F 0)
    rw [sub_add_cancel] at hn
    simp only [sub_zero,w.property,mul_one] at hb
    change ‖F w.1‖ ≤ B
    dsimp [B]
    linarith

steps.title: Pass from chords to angular cost
steps.text: The canonical angular-geometry result supplies measurability, nonnegativity, the pi upper bound and chord domination. Consequently K is M1 Lipschitz with respect to the actual angular cost.
steps.lean:
have hAng := AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Geometry.UnitSphereAngularCost.unit_sphere_angular_cost_properties (E := E)
  change Continuous c ∧ Measurable c ∧
    (∀ u v : S, 0 ≤ c (u,v) ∧ c (u,v) ≤ Real.pi ∧
      c (u,v) = InnerProductGeometry.angle u.1 v.1 ∧ ‖u.1-v.1‖ ≤ c (u,v) ∧
      (c (u,v) = 0 ↔ u = v) ∧ c (u,v) = c (v,u)) ∧
    ∀ u v w : S, c (u,w) ≤ c (u,v)+c (v,w) at hAng
  have hc0 (z : S × S) : 0 ≤ c z := (hAng.2.2.1 z.1 z.2).1
  have hcB (z : S × S) : c z ≤ Real.pi := (hAng.2.2.1 z.1 z.2).2.1
  have hKlip (w u : S) : ‖K w-K u‖ ≤ M₁*c (w,u) :=
    (hChord w.1 u.1 w.property.le u.property.le).trans
      (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hAng.2.2.1 w u).2.2.2.1 hM₁)

steps.title: Control actual means over all couplings
steps.text: Apply bounded Bochner transport to actual probability laws, not chosen optimal couplings. It produces integrability, finite Q, the mean difference estimate and the residual budget R0=B+norm(y).
steps.lean:
have hMean (μ ν : Measure S) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] [IsProbabilityMeasure ν] :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.BochnerMeanTransport.bounded_bochner_mean_quadratic_transport_control
      K hKsm B Real.pi M₁ hB Real.pi_pos.le hM₁ hKb c hAng.2.1 hc0 hcB hKlip μ ν
  have hTangent :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Geometry.QuadraticFeatureTangentGradient.quadratic_feature_potential_tangent_gradient
      F D hF M₁ M₂ hM₁ hM₂ hBound hLip
  let R₀ := B+‖y‖
  have hR₀ : 0 ≤ R₀ := add_nonneg hB (norm_nonneg y)
  have hResidual (μ : Measure S) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] : ‖m μ-y‖ ≤ R₀ :=
    ((hMean μ μ).2.2.2.2 y).1

steps.title: Identify the full ambient gradient
steps.text: For fixed residual r=m_mu-y the canonical scalar-potential derivative is 2 inner(D(w)*r,·). The real Riesz identification turns it into HasGradientAt, at every ambient weight rather than only unit points.
steps.lean:
have hGrad (μ : Measure S) (w : E) :
      HasGradientAt (V μ) ((2 : ℝ) • (D w).adjoint (m μ-y)) w := by
    rw [hasGradientAt_iff_hasFDerivAt]
    have he : InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ E ((2 : ℝ) • (D w).adjoint (m μ-y)) =
        (2 : ℝ) • innerSL ℝ ((D w).adjoint (m μ-y)) := by
      ext v
      simp [InnerProductSpace.toDual_apply_apply,innerSL_apply_apply]
    rw [he]
    exact hTangent.1 (m μ-y) w

steps.title: Choose constants before the laws
steps.text: Projection contraction gives the pointwise bound, while R0 is independent of the parameter law. Choose strictly positive C1,C2 before quantifying over all laws and weights. The constants are not claimed dimension free.
steps.lean:
let A := 2*M₁^2
  let B₂ := 2*(M₂+2*M₁)*R₀
  have hA : 0 ≤ A := by dsimp [A]; positivity
  have hB₂ : 0 ≤ B₂ := by dsimp [B₂]; positivity
  refine ⟨2*M₁*R₀+1,A+B₂+1,by positivity,by positivity,?_,?_⟩
  · intro μ hμ
    let : IsProbabilityMeasure μ := hμ
    refine ⟨(hMean μ μ).1,hGrad μ,?_⟩
    intro w
    have ht := hTangent.2.1 (m μ-y) w.1 w.property
    refine ⟨ht.1,?_⟩
    exact ht.2.2.trans ((mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hResidual μ) (by positivity)).trans (by linarith))

steps.title: Combine law and point movement
steps.text: Use the tangent-field joint estimate, substitute the actual mean sensitivity and residual budget, and dominate the chord by the angle. All costs are finite before applying toReal; the sum of the two coefficients plus one yields a single constant.
steps.lean:
· intro μ ν hμ hν
    let : IsProbabilityMeasure μ := hμ
    let : IsProbabilityMeasure ν := hν
    refine ⟨(hMean μ ν).2.2.1,?_⟩
    intro w u
    have hm : ‖(m μ-y)-(m ν-y)‖ ≤ M₁*(Q μ ν ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)).toReal := by
      simpa only [sub_sub_sub_cancel_right] using (hMean μ ν).2.2.2.1
    have hr := hResidual ν
    have ht := hTangent.2.2 (m μ-y) (m ν-y) w.1 u.1 w.property u.property
    have hpoint := (hAng.2.2.1 w u).2.2.2.1
    have ht' : ‖G μ w.1-G ν u.1‖ ≤
        A*(Q μ ν ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)).toReal+B₂*c (w,u) := by
      calc
        _ ≤ 2*M₁*‖(m μ-y)-(m ν-y)‖+
            2*(M₂+2*M₁)*‖m ν-y‖*‖w.1-u.1‖ := ht
        _ ≤ 2*M₁*(M₁*(Q μ ν ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)).toReal)+
            2*(M₂+2*M₁)*R₀*c (w,u) := by
          gcongr
        _ = _ := by dsimp [A,B₂]; ring
    apply ht'.trans
    have hs : 0 ≤ (Q μ ν ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)).toReal := ENNReal.toReal_nonneg
    have hc := hc0 (w,u)
    nlinarith [mul_nonneg hA hc,mul_nonneg hB₂ hs]
